narrative.overview: A deep-ink laboratory bench for buying tech fast. The ground is near-black ink, panels lift one tonal step, and a single volt-lime signal marks everything that converts: price, primary action, focus. A second signal, cyan, belongs exclusively to the RAG advisor — citations, assistant identity, links — so shoppers learn that cyan means cited evidence and volt means buy. Typography pairs a squared technical display voice with a quiet body workhorse and a tabular mono reserved for data. Motion is one exponential ease-out, never bounce; empty states are first-class panels, not afterthoughts.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first ink ground, never pure black; muted tones tinted from the ink hue.
One conversion signal (volt), one advisor signal (cyan); they never compete.
Display type with instrument character; prices in tabular mono.
Flat panels at rest; glow and lift respond to state.
Tactile and confident components with visible focus and motion-safe delight.

rules.name: The Two Signals Rule
rules.body: Volt converts, cyan evidences. A screen element carries one signal at most; cyan never prices or sells.

rules.name: The Tinted Muted Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is tinted from the ink hue. Flat gray on color is a defect.

rules.name: The Price Voice Rule
rules.body: Amounts are always mono tabular. A price set in body type is unfinished.

rules.name: The Heading Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings carry their own weight; kickers and eyebrow labels above them are banned.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadow and glow answer state changes only.

dos: Do price every amount in mono tabulars via the price voice.
Do reserve volt for conversion and cyan for evidence on every screen.
Do theme browser surfaces (selection, caret, scrollbar, focus) from the palette.
Do draw icons as SVG; keep the star glyph for ratings where it is content.
Do honor reduced-motion across zoom, pop, shimmer and smooth scroll.
donts: Don't nest cards; compose sections with dividers and spacing.
Don't set display type in Inter or body type in the mono face.
Don't use emoji as icons, gradient text, glass decoration, or bounce easing.
Don't write kickers above headings or number sections that carry no sequence.
Don't let the LLM invent prices, stock, or guarantees — data comes from SQL or cited chunks.
